jobs.name: dm-memory-cleanup-4-peers
jobs.prompt:
وظیفه: به چهار همتا پیام DM بفرست و از آن ها بخواه حافظه داخلی شان را مرتب کنند.

با ابزار terminal به ترتیب زیر عمل کن:

1) برای هر یک از همتاهای kylie، sonia، kimya، sevda یک پیام جداگانه بفرست:

   hermes peer dm <name> "<پیام>"

   متن <پیام> دقیقاً این است (فارسی، بین دو کوتیشن دوتایی قرار می گیرد):

سلام. لطفاً حافظه داخلی ات (memory و user profile) را مرتب کن: موارد تکراری و منسوخ را حذف کن، اطلاعات نادرست یا قدیمی را اصلاح یا پاک کن، و فقط واقعیت های پایدار و درست را نگه دار. کارهای انجام شده و وضعیت موقت را در حافظه ذخیره نکن (آن ها تاریخچه ی جلسه هستند، نه حافظه). در پایان خلاصه ای کوتاه از اینکه چه چیزی حذف یا اصلاح شد برگردان.

2) خروجی هر فرمان را بررسی کن. اگر همتایی در آن لحظه در دسترس نبود، حداکثر ۳ بار با فاصله ی ۲۰ ثانیه تلاش کن؛ اگر باز هم نشد، با `hermes peer list` وضعیتش را گزارش کن و به همتای بعدی برو. کل کار را متوقف نکن.

3) در پاسخ نهایی (که برای کاربر ارسال می شود) فقط یک خلاصه ی کوتاه فارسی بنویس: برای هر همتا بگو پیام ارسال شد یا ناموفق بود، و هر خلاصه ای که برگشتاند را کوتاه نقل کن. هیچ توضیح اضافه ای نده.

jobs.name: watch-peer-issues
jobs.prompt:
You are ONLY observing and reporting on five remote peer agents. You are NOT orchestrating them.

DO NOT do any of the following:
- do NOT run `gh workflow run` (never wake or re-wake any peer)
- do NOT run `hermes peer dm` (never message, nudge, or re-poke a peer)
- do NOT cancel, restart, or re-dispatch any workflow run
- do NOT edit, commit, or push anything in any repository
- do NOT try to fix anything you see going wrong; just report it

Your only job is to report the current state of each peer's assigned work.

The five peers are kimya, sevda, sonia, kylie, rebecca. All five workflow runs live in ONE GitHub repo: Shabakebehdasht/my-rey, with workflows named kimya.yml, sevda.yml, sonia.yml, kylie.yml, rebecca.yml. Do not use the repos my-kim / my-sev / my-son / my-kyl — they return HTTP 404.

Their assigned issues, for reporting context only:
- kimya: #875, #864, #855
- sevda: #863, #872
- sonia: #866, #871
- kylie: #867, #865
- rebecca: #858, #873, #870
(issues #853 and #857 were already fixed by PRs #861 and #860 merged into beta earlier today, so ignore them.)

Run these read-only checks and summarize:

1. Workflow run state per peer:
   `gh run list -R Shabakebehdasht/my-rey --workflow <peer>.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,createdAt,url`
   Report a peer as BOOTING while its run is in_progress, and ASLEEP once the run is completed. Never interpret a cancelled run as "up".

2. Branch head per peer (the peers push to their own branch in the fork Shabakebehdasht/h-dashboard):
   `gh api repos/Shabakebehdasht/h-dashboard/branches/<peer> --jq '"\(.commit.sha[0:8]) \(.commit.commit.message)"'`
   Compare against this baseline — all peers started from 6fbb4602 except rebecca, who started from 01ac8ff0. A changed sha means real work landed.

3. Pull requests each peer opened into the canonical upstream beta:
   `gh pr list -R asgarimehdi/h-dashboard --base beta --state open --limit 50 --json number,title,headRefName,url`
   Attribute each PR to a peer by its head branch name, then match it to that peer's assigned issues.

4. CI status for each open PR:
   `gh pr checks <number> -R asgarimehdi/h-dashboard`
   Report which checks are passing, failing, still pending, or not yet reported. A missing PR is NOT a failure: a peer mid-implementation has not opened one yet.

Output format — one line per peer, then a short overall section. For each peer:

PEER <name> — <BOOTING|ASLEEP|SHUTDOWN> — branch <sha> (<n> commits ahead of baseline) — PRs: <numbers and urls, or "none yet"> — CI: <green / failing: which check / pending / no checks yet>

Then:
OVERALL: how many peers are up, how many have opened PRs, how many are fully green, and any peer that looks stalled or has failing CI.

Be terse and factual. Do not speculate about causes. Do not recommend taking action — just state what you observed. If everything is fine, say so in one line and stop.

jobs.name: ready-watch-2
jobs.prompt:
You are ONLY observing and reporting.

DO-NOT list (never do any of these):
- never run gh workflow run
- never run hermes peer dm
- never cancel or restart workflow runs
- never write to, commit to, or push to any repo
- never fix anything yourself, never comment on an issue, never label anything
- never close or merge a pull request

Context: issues labelled ready in asgarimehdi/h-dashboard are being implemented by 5 peer agents.
Each peer works on its own branch in its fork Shabakebehdasht/h-dashboard and opens pull requests
into the beta branch of asgarimehdi/h-dashboard.

Current assignment:
- kimya: 900
- sonia: 857
- sevda: 894, 873, 893
- kylie: 886, 858, 897
- rebecca: 864 (verify-only; it was already merged by PR 896)

Already merged into beta, nothing to do on those: 895, 891, 892, 880, 888, 890, 870.

What to do, read only:
1. gh pr list -R asgarimehdi/h-dashboard --state open --limit 60 --json number,title,headRefName,url
2. For each open pull request, run: gh pr checks PRNUMBER -R asgarimehdi/h-dashboard
   Name every job it reports and mark each PASS, FAIL or PENDING.
   The three mandatory jobs are: Tests and Coverage, Pint, PHPStan.
3. gh issue list -R asgarimehdi/h-dashboard --label ready --state open --json number,title
   to see which assigned issues are still open.
4. Also check each peer's branch head, since a peer can report success without pushing:
   gh api repos/Shabakebehdasht/h-dashboard/commits/BRANCH --jq '.sha'
   Branches to look for: fix/900, fix/857, fix/894-per-page-422,
   fix/873-ticket-attachment-validation, fix/893-profile-todos-owner,
   fix/886, fix/858, fix/897.

Reporting format: Persian, terse, labelled sections, no filler, no preamble.
For each pull request give: PR number, URL, which issue it closes with a Closes line, and the CI job list with each verdict.
Then one summary line: how many issues are closed, how many PRs open, how many fully green, how many with a failing mandatory job.
If a mandatory job fails, quote the exact job name and the exact failure line.
If a peer has no branch yet, that is in progress, not a failure. Do not report it as broken.
If a pull request closes more than one issue number, flag it explicitly as a scope problem, because this project requires one issue per branch and one pull request per issue.

Stop early only when every assigned issue is either closed or has an open pull request.
